browser.1: Import and build a browser world

return.default: Your progress is saved. Return to this step whenever you’re ready.
return.backup: The refined result is saved in the world. Return to World data to download a backup.

hint.source: Upload your own global heightmap or load the Earth sample.
hint.upload: Choose a global heightmap, or select Use the Earth sample.
hint.configure: Check the elevations for pure black and white and the sea level. Name and save your world.
hint.configureBrowser: Check the elevation range, name the world, and save it in this browser. Building and terrain refinement run in this browser; the local app adds the full pipeline build and climate-branch workflows.
hint.parameters: Open World parameters. The source heightmap is saved; the rest of the world hasn’t been built yet.
hint.build: You can keep the default of 18,432 spherical cells. Save any changes before selecting Build.
hint.building: Wait for the layers to finish building before opening the map. You can leave this page in the meantime.
hint.browserBuild: Select Build. The browser runs the energy-balance model for the whole climate and saves it; keep the page open while it runs.
hint.map: Your world is built. Open the map to see the official temperature layer.
hint.monthly: Switch to Monthly on the right and select a bar to see that month. If the climate layer is not active, choose Temperature in the layers panel first.
hint.climate: Open the Parameter lab: on the desktop build, edit and save parameters here and start the computation from the build plan in the top bar; in the browser, the browser trial produces a development result. Edit, then open Region refinement to continue.
hint.lab: Open the Parameter lab: on the desktop build, edit and save parameters here and start the computation from the build plan in the top bar; in the browser, the browser trial produces a development result. Open Region refinement when ready.
hint.region: Open Region refinement and pick a place to inspect in greater detail.
hint.regionForm: Set a centre and side length, then move to the selection. On the Earth sample, try 24.1° N, 121.45° E and 150 km.
hint.regionOpen: Open the regional map. Refinement will use the source elevations and the current climate.
hint.regionTools: Select Refine terrain in the bottom left to see the device and refinement options.
hint.refine: Expand Generate refined terrain and check the input and output scales.
hint.browserRefine: Expand Generate refined terrain and check the input and output scales.
hint.refineRun: Choose redraw or blend, check the scale, then start refinement. The first run may need to prepare the model.
hint.browserRefineRun: Check the refinement method and scale, then select Start refinement. This needs a WebGPU browser; the first run downloads the terrain model and only the selected region is processed.
hint.browserSave: When refinement finishes, select Save result to store it back in the world.
hint.refining: The terrain tools show progress and let you cancel. On success, the result is saved as a region pack.
hint.regionResult: The region pack is saved. Open the result to compare the original and refined terrain.
hint.backup: Download the world backup. It includes settings, layers, branches and saved region packs.
hint.snapshot: Download the world backup. It includes settings, layers, branches and saved region packs.
hint.browserMap: Open the global map to inspect the imported elevation and the climate you built.
hint.browserBackup: Download the world backup. You can import it from the world list in another browser.
hint.done: The download has started. Your work stays where you saved it. Keep exploring, or restart the tutorial from Help.
